saints.name: St. Justin Martyr
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A philosopher who found in Christ the true wisdom he had long sought, and sealed his teaching with his blood…
biography: Born of pagan parents at Flavia Neapolis in Samaria about the year 100, Justin studied the schools of Greek philosophy until an encounter with an old man by the sea led him to the Scriptures and to faith in Christ. He continued to wear the philosopher's cloak, teaching the Gospel as the one sure philosophy, and opened a school at Rome.

His First and Second Apologies, addressed to the emperor, and his Dialogue with Trypho the Jew are among the earliest and most valuable defenses of the faith. Denounced as a Christian, he was scourged and beheaded at Rome about 165 under the prefect Rusticus, together with several companions.
saints.knownFor: His Apologies defending the faith to the pagan world.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
